info.name: TriloPlan User API
info.description:
Backend API surface for the User app — screen-verified against the User app's Figma (~90 screens, User app design follow-up). See CLAUDE.md, BACKEND_PLAN.md and BRD.md in the repo for full backend context.

Companion collections: `TriloPlan-Host.postman_collection.json` and `TriloPlan-Admin.postman_collection.json`.

## Four Figma/BRD conflicts resolved before building this pass
See `BACKEND_PLAN.md`'s "User app design follow-up" section for full detail. In short: the User app shows real currency (₹) only — every user-side amount is integer paise (render as paise / 100); beans are host-only; VIP Subscriptions were built despite BRD's prior "out of scope" call; "Level Up" loyalty tiers were **not** built (not in the BRD, no economics specified); Users verify age via self-declared DOB (`POST /me/verify-age`), Hosts still go through KYC review.

## OTP login while there's no real SMS yet
The backend has a dev-only bypass (`OTP_BYPASS_VERIFICATION=true` in the server's `.env`, off in production): `POST /auth/otp/verify` accepts ANY phone + ANY 6-digit code, no prior `/otp/request` call required. This collection still calls `/otp/request` first and saves `devCode` (harmless either way).

## Recommended run order (Collection Runner-safe, top to bottom)
Auth — User Login → Profile (Me) → Setup — Counterpart Host → Hosts — Discovery & Follow → Wallet → Wallet Recharge → VIP Subscription → Calls → Chat → Gifts → Live Broadcasting → Moderation → Grievance → Auth — Session → Delete Account (last — scrubs the account, so re-running the collection from the top afterward just creates a fresh one on the same `userPhone`).

item.name: Wallet Recharge
item.description: The Talktime/Add-balance screens' real flow — order creation against a preset package, then a dev-stubbed gateway confirmation (no real payment gateway wired up yet, BACKEND_PLAN.md §3).

request.description: Creates the recharge and, when the backend has Cashfree configured, a Cashfree order. Response adds paymentSessionId + checkoutMode ("sandbox"/"production") — the app passes them to Cashfree checkout (cashfree.js). Both are null without Cashfree (dev-stub — use step 4).
The app polls this after checkout. For a Cashfree recharge it re-checks the order with Cashfree first, so it flips to success (and credits the wallet, exactly once) even if the webhook is late.
Fakes the payment outcome without Cashfree — non-prod only. outcome can also be "failed" ("Payment failed" screen).

item.name: VIP Subscription
item.description: BRD.md's "Out of scope (this phase)" scope call on subscriptions was reversed by explicit decision (User app design follow-up) — see BACKEND_PLAN.md. Real benefit: a discount on call rates, applied automatically in Calls → Initiate Call below once subscribed.

exec: var threeMonth = jsonData.plans.find(function (p) { return p.name === "3 Months"; });

request.description: Starts a PAID purchase: returns { id, status: "created", amountPaise, paymentSessionId, checkoutMode, subscriptionId: null }. VIP is NOT active yet — it activates once the payment is confirmed (Cashfree webhook, or Get VIP Purchase Status after checkout). Paying again while active extends from the current expiry.
Polled after checkout — re-checks the Cashfree order and activates VIP once paid. subscriptionId is set once active.
Fakes the payment outcome without Cashfree — non-prod only. outcome can also be "failed".

Sets cancelAtPeriodEnd — benefits (incl. the call-rate discount) continue until expiresAt, matching the Active Subscriptions screen's copy. Run BEFORE Calls below if you want to see the un-discounted rate instead.

type is "video" or "voice" — the host needs the matching per-type rate set (Setup folder only sets the video rate). If VIP Subscription → Subscribe ran above and wasn't cancelled, the snapshotted rate reflects the VIP discount. mediaProvider ("agora" | "p2p") says which network carries this call's media — admin-switchable (Admin → Pricing & Economics Config → Call Media Provider), fixed per call once created. "agora": join with agoraToken (iceServers is null). "p2p": connect directly with browser WebRTC using iceServers (agoraToken is null), exchanging setup messages via POST .../calls/:id/signal — see REALTIME_EVENTS.md call:signal. Media: mediaProvider is "agora" (use agoraToken) or "p2p" (use iceServers). agoraFallbackAllowed: true means this p2p call may switch to Agora if the direct connection can't be made (2c. Fall Back to Agora).
durationQuality: "bad" (under 4 min), "good" (4–10 min) or "excellent" (over 10 min) for a finished call; null if it never connected or is still going.

p2p calls only — relays WebRTC setup to the other participant as the call:signal socket event (204, no body). data is one of { "type": "hello" }, { "type": "offer" | "answer", "sdp": "..." }, or { "type": "candidate", "candidate": { candidate, sdpMid, sdpMLineIndex, usernameFragment } }. Returns 409 when this call uses Agora (the default provider) — both outcomes are expected here, depending on the current Call Media Provider setting. The apps send these automatically (lib/p2p.js); this request is for inspecting the endpoint.

exec: pm.test("204 for a p2p call, 409 for an Agora call", function () { pm.expect([204, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: For calls with agoraFallbackAllowed: true (admin call media mode "auto") whose direct p2p connection couldn't be established. Moves the ongoing call to Agora and returns { callId, channelName, mediaProvider: "agora", agoraToken, iceServers: null, agoraFallbackAllowed }; the other participant gets the call:media-fallback socket event with its own token. Safe to call from both sides. 409 if the call isn't ongoing or isn't an auto call — the expected outcome when running this collection on the default Agora setting.

exec: pm.test("200 for an ongoing auto call, 409 otherwise", function () { pm.expect([200,409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Ends a still-ringing call as "missed" if the host never accepted — fine for exercising the endpoint.

Sent once by the app when a call ends — connection quality for the admin p2p-vs-Agora comparison. Only connected is required; relayed applies to p2p calls (true = went through the TURN relay). 204, no body; a repeat for the same call is ignored. 409 if the call never connected (e.g. it was missed) — the expected outcome when the host never accepted in this collection's run.

exec: pm.test("204 for a connected call, 409 if it never connected", function () { pm.expect([204,409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Only succeeds once the call has reached "completed" — will 409 if run right after End Call above left it "missed".

Past Calls screen. Returns { calls, total, page, pageSize, hasMore }; each call is the raw call record. filter: all (default) | video | voice | missed. page starts at 1; pageSize max 50 (default 20). Newest first. hasMore tells you whether to load the next page. durationQuality: "bad" (under 4 min), "good" (4–10 min) or "excellent" (over 10 min) for a finished call; null if it never connected or is still going.

Paid: each message to a host costs that host's message price (Level 1 = ₹5, +₹20 per host level; see messageRatePaise on Get Host Detail). Response adds chargedPaise and userBalanceAfterPaise. 402 "Insufficient wallet balance" if the user can't cover it — the message is not stored or delivered.
Newest first. Every message has type: "text" or "gift"; gift messages also have gift: { id, name, iconUrl } (null on text messages) and empty content.
image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp. Returns { uploadUrl (presigned PUT, 5 min), mediaKey, expiresIn: 300 }. Refused for anyone you can't message.
PUT the photo bytes to uploadUrl with the same Content-Type. The S3 bucket's CORS must allow PUT from both app origins.

exec: // The presigned URL is a whole URL with its own query string, so set it directly.

request.description: Charged like a text message. Returns the usual message with type "image" and mediaUrl (a signed GET valid ~1 h; history and chat:message carry a fresh one). 422 if automated image moderation blocks it (then nothing is sent or charged).

exec: pm.test("image with mediaUrl", function () { var j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.type).to.eql("image"); pm.expect(j.mediaUrl).to.be.a("string"); });

request.description: With context "chat": the gift also becomes a message in that conversation (created if none exists yet), in the same transaction as the charge — no per-message price on top. Response adds chatMessage: { messageId, conversationId, senderId, type: "gift", gift: { id, name, iconUrl }, content: "", createdAt } (null for other contexts), and the same object is pushed as chat:message to both people. contextId is ignored for chat — the real (user, host) conversation is always used.
"Not now" button on an in-call gift request — pushes gift:requestDeclined to the requesting host.

Response: { broadcastId, channelName, secureMode, mediaProvider, agoraToken, iceServers, pauseHiddenVideo }. mediaProvider "agora" → join the Agora channel with agoraToken. "cloudflare" → agoraToken is null; open an RTCPeerConnection with iceServers and run Watch via Cloudflare 1 (subscribe) + 2 (answer). pauseHiddenVideo: stop receiving video while the app is hidden.

"cloudflare" broadcasts only, after Join Broadcast. Returns { sessionId, sdp } — sdp is the SFU's offer of the host's tracks; set it as the remote description, create an answer and send it with Watch via Cloudflare 2. 409 while the host hasn't published yet (retry, or wait for live:media-updated), or when the broadcast uses Agora — the expected outcome on the default setting.

exec: pm.test("200 for a cloudflare broadcast, 409 otherwise", function () { pm.expect([200,409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Completes the viewer's SFU session with the app's SDP answer to the offer from step 1. 204, no body. 403 if sessionId isn't this viewer's current session; 409 when the broadcast uses Agora — the expected outcome on the default setting.

exec: pm.test("204 for a cloudflare broadcast, 403/409 otherwise", function () { pm.expect([204,403,409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

item.name: Support Chat
item.description: The User app's support chat — same endpoints as the Host app's, each account only ever sees its own tickets. Messages from the user have sender "user"; replies come from "bot" (the automatic assistant) or "agent" (a person on the support team). ticket.needsAgent = true means the bot has handed the ticket to a person.

request.description: Returns { ticket, messages } with the first message (sender "user"). If the support bot is switched on (Admin → Support → Bot config) and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set on the server, the bot's reply arrives a few seconds later as a `support:message` socket event (sender "bot", senderName "Support assistant") — re-fetch the ticket to see it. It never arrives in this response. Optional refs: { callId, withdrawalId } — the call or withdrawal the ticket is about; must be your own. Tickets now also carry priority, role, requester, refs and assigneeId.
{ tickets: [ticket] }, newest activity first. Each ticket has status (open|closed), needsAgent and handoffReason.
{ ticket, messages: [{ id, sender: user|bot|agent, senderName, content, createdAt }] }, oldest message first. 404 for someone else's ticket.

Returns the saved message. Writing on a closed ticket reopens it. If the support bot is switched on (Admin → Support → Bot config) and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set on the server, the bot's reply arrives a few seconds later as a `support:message` socket event (sender "bot", senderName "Support assistant") — re-fetch the ticket to see it. It never arrives in this response.

item.name: Attach a Photo 3: Send Photo Message

request.description: content is optional when mediaKey is set. The same mediaKey field works on POST /me/support/tickets (a ticket opened with a photo). Messages return attachments: [{ type: "image", url }] — a fresh signed URL valid ~1 h each time.

item.name: Delete Account
item.description: Run LAST — revokes tokens and scrubs the account (name/email/dob/username -> null, phone -> a random placeholder), so nothing after this in a from-the-top re-run needs the old userAccessToken. Re-running the whole collection afterward creates a fresh account on the same userPhone, since delete freed it up.

item.name: 1. Re-login (tokens from Auth — Session may be stale)

request.description: Any 6-digit code works while OTP_BYPASS_VERIFICATION is on — re-establishes a fresh access token in case Auth — Session's Logout already revoked the old one.
"Type DELETE to confirm" screen.
